## Full current page content [cooking-basics]

# Cooking Basics

Fundamental techniques for preparing food at home.

## Heat Transfer

There are three primary methods of heat transfer in cooking: conduction (direct contact with a hot surface), convection (hot air or liquid circulation), and radiation (infrared energy from a grill or broiler).

## Timing

Most vegetables cook in 5–12 minutes depending on density. Root vegetables take longer than leafy greens. Proteins need internal temperature verification rather than time alone. The recommended safe internal temperature for poultry is 82 °C.


Bacteria multiply rapidly in the temperature "danger zone" between 5 °C and 63 °C. Food held within this range for more than two hours should be discarded. Refrigeration should be maintained below 5 °C at all times.

*(Source: examples/food-safety-update.md, ingested 2026-08-12)*

Time at temperature matters as much as total cooking time: cooked or perishable food left between 5 °C and 63 °C for over two hours is no longer considered safe, regardless of how it was cooked.

*(Source: examples/food-safety-update.md, ingested 2026-08-12)*

## New source material

Origin: examples/poultry-temperature-revision.md

# Safe Internal Temperatures — Poultry

## Revision Notice

The recommended safe internal temperature for poultry was revised from 82 °C to 74 °C in 2024, based on updated pathogen destruction research. All poultry products including chicken, turkey, and duck should reach an internal temperature of 74 °C before serving.
